linkedin.hook: Cross-margin architectures routinely fail when collateral accounting decouples from real-time pool liquidity.
linkedin.copy:
Pooled lending models on new execution layers frequently suffer from latency arbitrage and socialize bad debt during volatile drawdowns. With Blend v2 deploying verified pool mechanics on Soroban, yield-bearing b-tokens offer genuine capital efficiency, but only if the credit layer wrapping them avoids shared-state execution bottlenecks.

Vanna handles this through isolated SmartAccount sandboxes. Instead of routing debt positions through monolithic shared contracts, each account executes within an independent state container. By querying contract state via our Mercury indexer at ~320ms latency, Vanna monitors the 1.10x Health Factor floor in real time. Transactions settle at a deterministic 0.00014 XLM gas cost, preventing cascading liquidations from pricing out maintenance calls.

Formal verification guarantees state machine safety, but infrastructure latency dictates actual solvency. We have opened this architecture for stress testing on Stellar testnet. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

reddit.hook: Technical breakdown: Integrating Blend v2 b-tokens into isolated SmartAccounts on Soroban testnet
reddit.copy:
We just pushed our Blend v2 b-token integration to testnet and wanted to share the smart contract architecture, risk parameters, and failure modes we observed during testing.

Blend v2 pools allow composable yield-bearing positions via b-tokens. In a typical cross-margin protocol, integrating these tokens creates recursive call overhead and unpredictable gas spikes during market drawdowns. If liquidation transactions compete for block space while indexers lag, the protocol accrues bad debt.

To prevent this, Vanna isolates all leverage mechanics into individual SmartAccount contracts on Soroban. Each sandbox holds the user collateral and debt state separately. 

Key execution metrics on testnet:
- Transaction cost: 0.00014 XLM fixed gas per rebalance invocation
- State ingestion: ~320ms Mercury indexer latency for balance and position indexing
- Liquidation threshold: 1.10x Health Factor hard floor

Because the SmartAccount contract handles callbacks directly against Blend v2 pools, health factor calculation happens on-chain during execution rather than trusting off-chain bot assumptions. If an account drops below the 1.10x floor, partial liquidations kick in to restore the ratio without liquidating the entire underlying position.

Instructions to test on testnet:
1. Fund a Stellar testnet wallet via Friendbot.
2. Navigate to test.stellar.vanna.finance.
3. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox.
4. Mint mock collateral, deposit into Blend v2 pools, and trigger automated rebalancing.

We are looking for edge cases around state updates during extreme interest rate shifts. Drop your transaction hashes or contract trace logs below.

Disclosure: I am a core engineer building Vanna Protocol.
